problem.text: Facts an agent relies on change over time, arrive late, and come from sources that disagree.

capabilities.name: Sources and authority on every value
Typed profiles and per-type conflict policies

values.outcome: Know which value is current, without deleting the old one
values.why: The agent doesn't act on stale state, and can still answer 'what was it before?'

proof.claim: LongMemEval knowledge-update: 65/65, history questions 0/11 → 11/11 vs REPLACE
Later value supersedes and keeps history (3 backends)

values.outcome: A late record goes where it belonged instead of overwriting the present
values.why: An old ticket, a backfill or a delayed sync can't corrupt the current state

proof.claim: OpenAI → Google → Anthropic: late value lands in history

values.outcome: Genuine disagreement is exposed, not silently resolved
values.why: The agent doesn't invent a truth when sources conflict, or let a weaker source quietly overwrite a stronger one

proof.claim: Mode A A-02: open-ended stronger claim vs weaker later claim → conflict (kept as a deliberate disagreement)

values.outcome: Know where every value came from, and how much to trust it
values.why: You can explain, or challenge, why the agent believes something

values.outcome: Rebuild any past memory state from the event log
values.why: Debug how the agent's memory got into its current state

proof.claim: Replay reproduces live state across policies

values.outcome: Different kinds of memory resolve by their own rules (confidence guards, always-replace types)
values.why: A deadline and a birthplace shouldn't update the same way

proof.claim: Mode A typed category: typed core 1.00 (states 0.67)

values.outcome: Fewer production mistakes caused by stale facts
values.why: If stale facts drive wrong actions, V1–V3 should reduce them
